gaps.sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'How much does this cost?' I asked the vendor. I asked the vendor how much it ___.
gaps.explanation: does cost → cost: the past simple of 'cost' is 'cost', used with statement word order.

gaps.sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
gaps.explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

gaps.sentence: 'What are your plans for the weekend?' he asked. He asked what my plans for the weekend ___.
gaps.explanation: are → were: the copula backshifts like any other verb.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.
